hints: Focus on which common nitrogen gas can act as a base and neutralise an acid to make a salt.
Remember that $\text{NH}_3$ with nitric acid gives ammonium nitrate, so salt 1 must be an ammonium salt.
Think about warming that ammonium salt with sodium hydroxide alkali, and work out which sodium salt is left in solution.
walkthrough:
**Identify gas 1 from gas + acid to salt**

Only a basic gas will react directly with an acid to form a salt. Ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, does exactly this.

Chemical idea:
$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{acid} \rightarrow \text{ammonium salt}$$

**Work out what salt 1 is**

With nitric acid, the product is ammonium nitrate. This fits the nitrogen compounds theme.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$$
So salt 1 is $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$.

**React salt 1 with alkali to get salt 2**

Ammonium salts react with alkali such as $\text{NaOH}$ on warming to release ammonia again. The metal from the alkali replaces ammonium.

$$\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaNO}_3 + \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Salt 2 is therefore sodium nitrate, $\text{NaNO}_3$, with ammonia and water as other products.

options.A: Ammonia is correct for gas 1, but ammonium nitrate is salt 1, not salt 2. After reaction with sodium hydroxide alkali, the ammonium ion is converted to ammonia and the nitrate ends up as the sodium salt.
options.B: Gas 1 is ammonia because it neutralises acid to give an ammonium salt. Salt 1 is ammonium nitrate, and with NaOH alkali it gives sodium nitrate as salt 2 plus ammonia and water.
options.C: Nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, is incorrect for gas 1. It is an acidic gas and does not neutralise an acid to form an ammonium salt in this way. Ammonium nitrate is salt 1, not the final salt 2.
options.D: Nitrogen dioxide is incorrect for gas 1, even though sodium nitrate is correct for salt 2. The first step needs the basic gas ammonia to make an ammonium salt, not an acidic oxide.
